metadata.title: Nebula — A little closer to the stars
metadata.description: Super Mario Galaxy, native. See what’s coming in Nebula v2: ray tracing, smoother motion, controller support, mods and achievements. Bring your own game.

stats.title_1: Total GitHub release-asset downloads, not unique players.

available.paragraph_1: The latest public release for Windows. Bring your own copy of Super Mario Galaxy.

v2.paragraph_1: Nebula lets you play Super Mario Galaxy natively, using your own copy of the game. v2 adds ray-traced lighting, high-refresh motion, more controller options, mods and achievements.
v2.paragraph_2: The original adventure stays at the centre: the same levels, music and movement, with settings that fit your screen and the way you play.
v2.paragraph_3: Sunlight, shadows, reflections and water, with lamps, fire and Lumas lighting the world around them.
v2.paragraph_4: Extra frames follow the game’s own motion, bringing smoother movement to 75, 120, 144, 165, 240 Hz and other displays.
v2.paragraph_5: Internal resolution up to 16× and aspect ratios from 4:3 to 32:9, with sharp text and a HUD that fits your screen.
v2.paragraph_6: Keyboard and mouse, Xbox, PlayStation, Switch controllers, Joy-Con, Steam controllers and a real Wii Remote with Nunchuk.
v2.paragraph_7: Skip cutscenes, speed up dialogue and change settings from an in-game menu. Import Miis for your save-file icons.
v2.paragraph_8: Import Riivolution mods, file replacements, Dolphin-format texture packs and HD movies from the Mods menu or by drag and drop.
v2.paragraph_9: Track your progress with achievement pop-ups and a Luma’s board in the Comet Observatory, with goals and lifetime play stats.
v2.paragraph_10: Import a Dolphin save, back up your progress and move saves through the launcher. Your current saves are backed up before an import.

start.paragraph_1: For v2, you need Super Mario Galaxy for Wii, North America (RMGE01), revision 0. Prepare an ISO, RVZ or extracted game folder.
start.paragraph_2: Windows 10 / 11 (64-bit), an AVX2-capable CPU, a Direct3D 12 GPU, 8 GB RAM and about 5 GB of space.
start.paragraph_3: Choose your game, install, then open Nebula from the Start menu. The setup guide covers the steps and your first settings.

community.paragraph_1: Join Discord for v2 announcements, setup help and conversations with other players. Found a problem? Send a bug report with your version, settings and the steps to reproduce it.

questions.paragraph_1: Yes. Nebula is free software under the GNU GPL v3. You need your own copy of Super Mario Galaxy; game files are not included.
questions.paragraph_2: Not yet. v2 is coming soon. The current public release is v1.0.1. The v2 features described here are for the upcoming update.
questions.paragraph_3: No. In v2, Super Mario Galaxy runs as native code built from SMGCommunity’s Petari decompilation. The original levels, music, story and gameplay come from your own game.
questions.question_4: Which copy of the game do I need?
questions.paragraph_4: The supported copy is the North American Wii release, RMGE01, revision 0. For v2, prepare an ISO, RVZ or extracted folder. Support for other regions has not been announced.
questions.question_5: Can I play on Linux, Steam Deck, Android or Mac?
questions.paragraph_5: Windows is available now, and an Android beta is released. Linux and SteamOS are in development; macOS is planned.
questions.question_6: Can I use a Dolphin save?
questions.paragraph_6: Yes. Close the game, then use Advanced → Import saves in the launcher. See the save guide for the steps.
questions.paragraph_7: No. File replacements and compatible texture packs work, but mods that patch the Wii’s machine code may not run in a native game. Check the mod guide before importing.
questions.paragraph_8: No. Nebula is an independent project by the Nebula developers. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Nintendo.
